title_en: Zhang Zhiqing v. Feng Zhaoxia, Cui Feng, and Xinxiang Xinhua Comprehensive Service Co., Ltd. — tort dispute
ruling_gist_en: For cases occurring when the housing registration system was still incomplete and the parties did not conclude a written agreement, the determination of whether a house sale relationship exists shall be made by a comprehensive analysis based on the actual performance, taking into account whether the buyer paid consideration, whether the house value and the price paid are reasonable, whether the seller delivered the house and the house ownership certificate or the buyer has occupied the house for a long period, whether the seller claimed any rights during that period, and whether relationships such as borrowing or leasing can be excluded.

full_text_en:
Zhang Zhiqing v. Feng Zhaoxia, Cui Feng, and Xinxiang Xinhua Comprehensive Service Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement

Ruling Summary

For cases occurring at a time when the housing registration system was not yet complete, and where the parties did not enter into a written agreement, the existence of a housing sale relationship shall be determined by comprehensively analyzing and assessing the actual performance, including whether the buyer paid consideration, whether the housing value and the price paid were reasonable, whether the seller delivered the house and the title certificate or the buyer took long-term possession of the house, whether the seller claimed any rights during that period, and whether relationships such as borrowing or leasing can be ruled out.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 163

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Original Respondent): Zhang Zhiqing, female, Han ethnicity, born on September 15, 1936, residing at No. 44-1, Sanpai Fang Lane, Hongqi District, Xinxiang City, Henan Province.

Authorized Agent: Lei Jun, lawyer, Henan Guanghe Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Sun Hongliang, lawyer, Henan Guanghe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Applicant for Retrial): Feng Zhaoxia, female, Han ethnicity, born on November 11, 1972, residing at No. 16, Bungalow, 181 Renmin Road, Weibin District, Xinxiang City, Henan Province.

Defendant at First Instance: Cui Feng, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 16, 1971, residing at East Unit, 3rd Floor, Building 1, No. 18 Donggandao, Xinxiang City, Henan Province.

Defendant at First Instance: Xinxiang Xinhua Comprehensive Service Co., Ltd. (formerly Xinhua District Living Service Company). Domicile: No. 10 Xinyuan Street, Xinxiang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Shen Rongchun, Manager of the Company.

The applicant for retrial, Zhang Zhiqing, filed an application with this Court for retrial against the civil judgment (2010) Yu Fa Min Ti Zi No. 99 of the Henan High People's Court in the dispute over infringement with the respondent Feng Zhaoxia, and the defendants at first instance Cui Feng and Xinxiang Xinhua Comprehensive Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinhua Service Company). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review the case, and the review has now been concluded.

Zhang Zhiqing applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The original retrial judgment, which found that there was a housing sale relationship between Zhang Zhiqing and Xinhua Service Company, contained erroneous findings of fact and insufficient evidence. 2. The original retrial judgment's determination that Zhang Zhiqing, without reasonable grounds, failed to assert her rights for more than 20 years and thus lost ownership of the house was not only inconsistent with the facts but also erroneous in the application of law. 3. The original retrial judgment's finding that the evidence submitted by Feng Zhaoxia had greater probative value than the evidence on Zhang Zhiqing's side was entirely inconsistent with the facts and clearly biased. She requested a retrial of the case pursuant to Article 179, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Opinion of the Court:
The focal issue in this case is whether there was a housing sale relationship between Zhang Zhiqing and Xinhua Service Company. First, although Zhang Zhiqing and Xinhua Service Company did not enter into a written housing sale contract, Zhang Zhiqing acknowledged that when she transferred the disputed house to Xinhua Service Company in 1983, she received RMB 2,000. Zhang Zhiqing's father, Zhang Baoxing, had paid RMB 1,100 for the purchase of the house in 1982. Even considering that Zhang Baoxing had renovated the house, it is reasonable to regard the RMB 2,000 as the sale price for the house. Moreover, the house had been transferred to the use of others for over 20 years, and the consideration of RMB 2,000 is minimal compared to the fees payable for using the house for over 20 years. Since there was no agreement on the term of use when the RMB 2,000 was paid, and given the prevailing housing prices at that time, Zhang Zhiqing's assertion that the RMB 2,000 was a usage fee is unreasonable; that amount is roughly equivalent to the housing prices at that time and is more consistent with the nature of a purchase price. Second, in 1983, China's housing registration system was not yet complete, and it was common practice to transfer title documents rather than go through registration procedures when transferring property rights. When Zhang Zhiqing transferred the house to Xinhua Service Company for use, she also delivered the title deed (qi zhi) issued by the government, which could reflect her true intention to transfer the property right in the house. Finally, more than 20 years had passed from the time Zhang Zhiqing transferred the disputed house to Xinhua Service Company until she filed the lawsuit. The possession and use by Xinhua Service Company and Feng Zhaoxia were continuous, open, and peaceful. Zhang Zhiqing had not asserted any rights in this regard for over 20 years, indicating that she had no objection to others' possession and use of the house for a long period. If it were found that Zhang Zhiqing did not transfer the property right, her prolonged failure to exercise rights as the owner would sharply contrast with the general attention an owner would pay to his or her rights, which is clearly unreasonable. In summary, a housing sale relationship had been formed between Zhang Zhiqing and Xinhua Service Company, and that sale contract was valid and effective. Based on the valid contractual relationship, Zhang Zhiqing has no right to request the return of the house. The original retrial judgment's dismissal of Zhang Zhiqing's claim for the return of the house was not erroneous, and Zhang Zhiqing's grounds for the retrial application are untenable.

In conclusion, Zhang Zhiqing's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided for in Article 179, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Zhang Zhiqing is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Wang Huijun
Acting Judge: Wang Zhanfei
Acting Judge: Chen Lintai
December 29, 2010

Clerk: Yang Lichao

Introduction to the Presiding Judge
Wang Huijun, Senior Judge: Born in 1962, Bachelor of Laws, served as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court from 2004.
